newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Narrow Brent/Dubai prompts demand for Yemen crude.
newsitem.headline: Narrow Brent/Dubai prompts demand for Yemen crude.

text.p: A narrow price differential between Brent and Dubai crudes has boosted demand for Yemen's Masila and Marib Light grades, allowing Yemen to easily commit all its exports on term for the third quarter.
This was despite of a rise in Yemen's third quarter term price, traders said on Thursday.
Yemen finalised its third quarter crude term contracts last week, increasing total Masila term volumes by more than a quarter from 90,000 b/d in the second quarter.
The term price for Masila has been rising all year amid the Brent weakness, which emerged from the second quarter of the year.
Early last week, Yemen announced third quarter term prices.
Masila was set at dated Brent -35 cents per barrel, up from the second quarter price of dated Brent -50 and first quarter price of dated Brent -97 cents.
The Marib Light term price for the third quarter was set at dated Brent -10, up from dated Brent -15 in the second quarter and dated Brent -30 cents in the first quarter.

Most term customers of Masila agreed to renew their contracts into the third quarter, expecting the Brent/Dubai spread to remain narrow enough to keep Masila crude cheaper relative to other grades priced against Dubai.
Only U.S. oil group Chevron Corp and China's Sinochem declined to lift Masila in the third quarter. Sources at both companies said the companies considered the term price too high.
"The price is a factor," said a Sinochem company source.
"Our market view is that Brent will increase, and we think it would not be economic to lift in the third quarter," he said.
Sinochem bought 7,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Masila on term in the second quarter, while Chevron took 5,000 bpd.

Despite the hike in the term price, Japan's Cosmo Oil Co Ltd, France's Total SA and Neste Oy of Finland - who had declined to take term Masila in the second quarter - returned to resume their contracts for the third quarter, attracted by the narrow Brent/Dubai spread.
Cosmo had bought Masila on term in the first quarter of this year, but stopped in the second quarter due to difficulties in getting their desired loading dates.
"We wanted early loading dates, but were given later ones, which was frustrating," said a Cosmo source.
"But we regret not lifting in the second quarter because the Brent/Dubai spread was very narrow," he said.
In addition, Yemen attracted U.S. Coastal Corp and the Emirates National Oil Company (ENOC) as new Masila customers.
For Marib Light, Vitol was the only company who did not renew its term contracts in the third quarter, but its volumes were taken up by Total SA.

The 185,000 bpd Masila crude field is operated by Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, but the Yemeni government has a 115,000 bpd equity in the field which is marketed through the quarterly term contracts.
Hunt and Exxon Corp operate the 165,000 bpd Marib Light field, 115,000 bpd of which is the equity share of the Yemeni government.
The 170,000-bpd Aden Refinery and a small topping unit consumes 75,000 bpd of the government's share of Marib Light. The rest is exported.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3080)
